lines: Title: Identity Mapping is Complete Lattice Homomorphism
Let $\operatorname{id}_A$ denote the [[Definition:Identity Mapping|identity mapping]] on $A$.
:$\operatorname{id}_A$ is a [[Definition:Complete Lattice Homomorphism|complete lattice homomorphism]] of $L$ to $L$
It follows that $\operatorname{id}_A$ is [[Definition:Arbitrary Join Preserving Mapping|arbitrary join preserving]].
By definition of [[Definition:Arbitrary Join Preserving Mapping|arbitrary join preserving]]:
:$\forall X \subseteq A : \map {\operatorname{id}_A} {\sup A} = \sup \set{\map{\operatorname{id}_A} x : x \in X}$
By the [[Duality Principle (Order Theory)|duality principle]], the [[Definition:Dual Statement (Order Theory)|dual]] of this statement is:
:$\forall X \subseteq A : \map {\operatorname{id}_A} {\inf A} = \inf \set{\map{\operatorname{id}_A} x : x \in X}$
By definition of [[Definition:Arbitrary Meet Preserving Mapping|arbitrary meet preserving]]:
:$\operatorname{id}_A$ is [[Definition:Arbitrary Meet Preserving Mapping|arbitrary meet preserving]]
It follows that $\operatorname{id}_A$ is a [[Definition:Complete Lattice Homomorphism|complete lattice homomorphism]] by definition.
